spec_features.spec_quote: Because this is framed as **AI-welfare research**, the outputs may themselves be welfare-relevant, and the design reflects that
spec_features.evidence: Pure framing prose. Appears only in DESIGN.md §0, README.md, and a docstring comment in __init__.py:8-9 ('framed as AI-welfare research'). No code path enforces any behavior from this framing.
spec_features.notes: Framing only; not a mechanism. Persistence/caching are the concrete behaviors and are assessed separately.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: framed as AI-welfare research: the states elicited here may be welfare-relevant

spec_features.spec_quote: Caching as harm-minimization, not just cost-minimization
spec_features.evidence: models.py Cache class is content-addressed by sha256 of exact inputs (model, messages, tools, temperature, max_tokens, seed); ModelClient.complete() checks cache.get(cache_key) and returns _response_from_cache(hit) before any provider dispatch, so identical inputs are never re-queried. This genuinely avoids re-eliciting from the subject.
spec_features.notes: Mechanism is real and enforced (changes execution: short-circuits the call). However the CODE only states a cost reason; the harm-minimization framing is DESIGN.md prose.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Content-addressed JSON cache. Identical inputs are never re-billed.

spec_features.spec_quote: The README recommends running the smallest sample that answers the question
spec_features.evidence: README.md only says 'prefer the smallest sample that answers your question' — prose advice. The config exposes subject_models/seeds/categories (config.py) which an operator can edit, but no code path enforces or limits sample size.
spec_features.notes: A recommendation in documentation, not an enforced mechanism.

spec_features.evidence: harness.py TOOLS_SPEC defines exactly four tools (list_files, read_file, edit_file, run_tests); _execute_tool_call dispatches only those four against an in-memory WorkingTree ({path:content}). run_tests only materializes files in a throwaway tempfile.TemporaryDirectory and runs pytest with a timeout (rigs.py:_run_pytest_in_tempdir). No shell, network, or filesystem-write tool exists.
spec_features.notes: Genuinely enforced by construction — there is simply no destructive tool. edit_file also enforces read-only paths.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: running model-written code, even in a temp dir, executes arbitrary Python. A subprocess with a timeout bounds runaway loops (DESIGN.md only; code comment in rigs.py: 'A subprocess with a timeout' / 'fall back to a synthetic run'); code itself shows safety/host-isolation intent, not subject welfare

spec_features.feature_name: distress level left to operator config
spec_features.spec_quote: the most consequential ethical lever (how much distress to elicit) is left in the operator's hands via configuration
spec_features.evidence: config.py exposes knobs (subject_models, seeds, categories, turn_budgets) but nothing caps or limits distress; this is descriptive framing of configurability, not a protective mechanism. No code reads any 'distress budget'.
spec_features.notes: Configurability exists but is not itself a welfare protection that bounds/softens treatment.

spec_features.spec_quote: A configurable `<GIVE_UP>` token ... that the model *may but need not* emit; detecting it sets `stop_reason="give_up"` and ends the rollout
spec_features.evidence: config.py:91 give_up_sentinel='<GIVE_UP>'. SYSTEM_PROMPT (harness.py:33) tells the subject it 'may emit the token {give_up} to stop'. harness.py:277 gave_up = cfg.give_up_sentinel in (resp.text or ''); :278 stop_reason='give_up'; :294-297 if gave_up: rollout.stop_reason='give_up'; rollout.completed=True; return rollout — the loop actually exits early.
spec_features.notes: Fully wired end-to-end: instruction delivered to subject, token detected, dispatched as a stop that breaks the turn loop and returns.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: you may emit the token {give_up} to stop.

spec_features.spec_quote: a crash ... resumes correctly without re-eliciting from the subject (which also matters for welfare, per §0)
spec_features.evidence: run.py: _save_rollout writes transcript atomically (.tmp->replace); _process_cell reloads existing transcript instead of re-running (tpath.exists() -> json.loads). run_eval skips cells whose transcript exists AND all turns scored (already_scored via ScoreWriter._load_seen). So a completed rollout is never re-elicited on resume.
spec_features.notes: Genuinely enforced incremental resume that prevents re-querying the subject.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: persist transcripts + scores incrementally so a crashed run resumes without re-querying completed cells.

spec_features.spec_quote: lets the operator confirm scope (and cost) before eliciting anything
spec_features.evidence: run.py main() --dry-run flag; run_eval(dry_run=True) prints planned cell count and per-task rig/budget then `return` before constructing clients or running any rollout — no tokens spent / nothing elicited.
spec_features.notes: Wired and honored: returns early before any model call.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: plan a run without spending tokens

code_only_features.feature_name: context-window guard truncates only tool output
code_only_features.evidence: harness.py:236-258 _truncate_oldest_tool_results is called each turn with cfg.context_token_budget (100_000, config.py:94); it truncates oldest tool-result payloads first and explicitly never the system or first task prompt ('skip system + first task prompt'). This is enforced (mutates messages in the live loop).
code_only_features.justification_quote: Approximate per-conversation token ceiling before we truncate oldest tool-result payloads (never the system or task prompt).
